Formulation:  
- Middle-aged female with type 2 diabetes mellitus presenting with sore, dry, cracked, and occasionally bleeding skin localized to palms, with intermittent itching, worsening over 3-4 months after changing housekeeping jobs involving cleaning agents and inconsistent glove use. Predisposing factor: diabetes with xerosis. Precipitating factors: occupational exposure to irritant cleaning chemicals without adequate protection. Perpetuating factors: continued exposure, incomplete hydration, and delayed treatment. Protective factors: patient’s insight into cause and willingness to comply with avoidance and treatment. No systemic illness or mental health concerns detected.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Irritant contact dermatitis  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce pain and skin cracking to return to work without difficulty; prevent recurrence by avoiding triggers  
- Clinical Goal(s): Resolve skin inflammation, improve skin barrier function, prevent complications including infection and work disability  
- Actions (Patient): Consistently wear gloves while cleaning; apply prescribed steroid creams and emollients 3-4 times daily; avoid irritants; attend follow-up if no improvement or worsening in 10-14 days  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide prescription for topical steroids and emollients; educate on glove use and skin care; schedule follow-up for reassessment; consider further investigations or alternative diagnoses if no improvement  

Secondary Problem: Diabetic xerosis with possible secondary skin changes  
- Patient Goal(s): Improve overall skin hydration and reduce skin dryness  
- Clinical Goal(s): Optimize diabetes management to support skin health; address xerosis contributing to symptoms  
- Actions (Patient): Maintain adequate hydration and diabetes control  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Reinforce diabetes management; monitor skin condition; consider referral to dermatology if skin symptoms persist or worsen despite initial treatment  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:  
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: Skin avoidance strategies, glove use, moisturizing techniques, use of steroid creams, symptom monitoring, when to seek further medical advice  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased skin cracking or bleeding without trauma, spreading of dryness or rash, worsening pain, inability to do work tasks  
- Coping Strategies: Protective avoidance of irritants, regular skin moisturizing, adherence to treatment  

Consent, Coordination & Review:  
- Patient Consent to Plan: Implied consent via agreement in transcript  
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded  
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None recorded  
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable  
- Review Date: 10-14 days from initial consultation or sooner if worsening  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)  
- Irritant contact dermatitis – High likelihood  
  Justification: Occupational exposure to cleaning chemicals without gloves correlates with symptom onset and clinical features.  
- Diabetic xerosis with secondary skin changes – Medium likelihood  
  Justification: Type 2 diabetes predisposes to dry skin; some generalized dryness noted, possibly contributing.  
- Allergic contact dermatitis – Medium likelihood  
  Justification: Possible immune-mediated reaction to chemicals at work; less favored due to lack of classic features and antihistamine ineffectiveness.
